blocks.headline: 1a Deutsch international
blocks.bodyEnglish:
Many German words are used in other languages.
Match each foreign word to the German word — that is exercise 1a.

blocks.title: Deutsch international
blocks.bodyEnglish:
Many German words are used in other languages.
You may already know some of them.
Think of kindergarten, Autobahn and Handtuch.
blocks.bodyGerman:
der Kindergarten
die Autobahn
das Handtuch

blocks.headline: 2 Hallo! Tschüs!
blocks.bodyEnglish: Julia and Niklas meet. They say hello, ask how they feel, and then say goodbye.

vocabHighlight.english: How are you? — a friendly question
Thanks, very good. — a positive answer
And you? — ask the same question back

turns.speaker: Julia
turns.german: Hallo, ich bin Julia. Und du? Wer bist du?
turns.english: Hello, I am Julia. And you? Who are you?

blocks.title: Informell: Hallo, Tschüs, Ciao
blocks.bodyEnglish:
Hallo and Tschüs are informal.
Use them with friends and with first names.
Ciao comes from Italian.

blocks.headline: heißen und sein
blocks.bodyEnglish:
Two verbs introduce you: heißen means be called, sein means be.
The rule card below gives every form for every person.

blocks.ruleHeadline: sein: ich bin, du bist, er/sie/es ist …
blocks.explanationEnglish:
sein means be. It is irregular, so learn the six forms as one block.
The full row: ich bin, du bist, er/sie/es ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie/Sie sind.
Every person has its own word. There is no ending to add.
Trap: English uses are for almost every person. German does not.
Capital Sie is the polite form. It always takes sind, like sie (they).
blocks.englishBridge: English you are covers two words: du bist (informal) and Sie sind (formal).
blocks.targetSentenceGerman: Ich bin Julia. Sie sind neu hier.
blocks.targetSentenceEnglish: I am Julia. You are new here.

blocks.ruleHeadline: heißen: ich heiße, du heißt, er/sie heißt
blocks.explanationEnglish:
heißen means be called. It gives your name.
The stem is heiß-. Add the ending of the person: ich -e, du -t, er/sie -t.
All six forms: ich heiße, du heißt, er/sie heißt, wir heißen, ihr heißt, sie/Sie heißen.
The du-form ends in -t, not -st: after ß the ending -st becomes -t.
Trap: ich needs its -e: ✗ Ich heiß Nina. → ✓ Ich heiße Nina.
blocks.englishBridge: English uses call; German uses heißen: Ich heiße Niklas = I am called Niklas.
blocks.targetSentenceGerman: Ich heiße Niklas. Wie heißen Sie?
blocks.targetSentenceEnglish: My name is Niklas. What is your name?

examples.english: they are called / you are called (formal)

blocks.title: Sich vorstellen
blocks.explanationEnglish: Present yourself with heißen plus a name. sein plus a name works too. All three forms are correct.
After ich, heißen takes the ending -e: ich heiße. The du-form is du heißt.

concept.title: heißen
concept.rule: heißen: ich heiße · du heißt · er/sie heißt · Sie heißen. The ending marks the person.

blocks.explanationEnglish: geht belongs to the fixed phrase Wie geht's. ich of sein is bin. The answer word is gut.

concept.title: Nach dem Befinden fragen
concept.rule: Ask: Wie geht's? Answer: Danke, sehr gut. / Danke, gut. / Ganz gut. Then ask back: Und dir?
concept.exampleEnglish: How are you? — Thanks, very good!

blocks.explanationEnglish: The subject comes first, then the verb, then the name. ich takes the ending -e.

concept.title: Aussagesatz mit heißen
concept.rule: A statement has three parts: subject, verb, name. Ich heiße Niklas.
